name: XL1509-5.0E1
title: XL1509: 2 A, 150 kHz, 40 V step-down DC-DC converter in SOIC8
summary: A non-synchronous buck regulator with its power switch inside, running at a fixed 150 kHz from 4.5 V to 40 V and delivering up to 2 A through an external inductor and Schottky catch diode. It comes in fixed 3.3 V, 5 V and 12 V versions and an adjustable version whose 1.23 V feedback reference sets outputs from 1.23 V to 37 V; the XL1509-5.0E1 is the 5 V part. Duty cycle reaches 100 %, loop compensation is internal, an active-low ON/OFF input that has hysteresis shuts it down, and it has current limiting, a second current limit that drops the switching frequency to 50 kHz, and thermal shutdown.

notes: The code reads XL1509, then the version (ADJ, 3.3, 5.0 or 12), then E1. E1 marks a lead-free, RoHS-compliant part. The part number is also the marking.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 4.5 V to 40 V. It takes a bypass capacitor to GND large enough to suppress input noise.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Switch node (SW): the internal power switch connects it to VIN to drive the inductor.

pins.name: FEEDBACK
pins.function: Feedback (FB). On the adjustable version an external resistor divider from the output sets the voltage against the 1.23 V threshold; on fixed versions it connects to the output.

pins.name: ON/OFF
pins.function: Enable, active low: low runs the regulator, high shuts it down. Left open it reads as low.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground. Its connection stays out of the ground path from the Schottky diode to the output capacitor, so switching-current spikes do not couple noise into the part.

circuits.title: Typical application, 12 V to 5 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 5 V part steps a 12 V supply down to 5 V for a 2 A load. When the internal switch conducts, OUTPUT connects the 68 µH inductor to the input; when it opens, the 1N5820 Schottky carries the inductor current from ground. FEEDBACK goes straight to the 5 V rail, since the divider is inside. CIN is the bulk input electrolytic and C1 (code 105, 1 µF) sits beside it; COUT smooths the output. ON/OFF is the control input: low runs the converter, high turns it off. The same circuit is the one the 5 V version's output and efficiency figures are measured in.

circuits.title: 3.3 V version, 12 V to 3.3 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 3.3 V part converting 12 V to 3.3 V at 2 A; it is also the circuit the 3.3 V version's output and efficiency figures are measured in. The power path is the same as the 5 V circuit, with a 47 µH inductor and a 330 µF output capacitor. FEEDBACK senses the output directly; ON/OFF low enables the part.

circuits.title: 12 V version, 24 V to 12 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 12 V part converting 24 V to 12 V at 2 A, and the measuring circuit for that version's figures. The input capacitor is rated 50 V and the catch diode is the 30 V 1N5821; FEEDBACK goes straight to the 12 V output and ON/OFF low enables the part.

circuits.title: Adjustable version, 24 V to 5 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The adjustable part converting 24 V to 5 V at 2 A, and the measuring circuit for that version. R2 (3.1 kΩ) from the output and R1 (1 kΩ) to ground divide the output onto FEEDBACK, so VOUT = 1.23 × (1 + R2/R1), about 5 V. CFF across R2 is the feedforward capacitor that adds loop stability. The power path is a 47 µH inductor, a 1N5821 Schottky and a 470 µF output electrolytic; ON/OFF low enables the part.

circuits.title: Standard test circuit, fixed output versions
circuits.description: The circuit the fixed versions are characterised in, with layout rules: an unregulated input with CIN and a 1 µF C1 at the VIN and GND pins, the switch node to L1 and the catch diode D1, and FEEDBACK returned to the regulated output. The feedback trace runs clear of the inductor's magnetic field; the heavy current paths stay short over a ground plane.

circuits.title: Standard test circuit, adjustable version
circuits.description: The adjustable version's characterisation circuit: as the fixed one, with R1 (1 kΩ) from FEEDBACK to ground and R2 from FEEDBACK to the output setting VOUT = 1.23 × (1 + R2/R1), and the optional CFF across R2. R1 and R2 sit close to the FEEDBACK pin on short leads, and the feedback trace keeps away from the inductor's field.

circuits.title: Optional output ripple filter
circuits.description: An LC stage after the regulated output to cut ripple further: a 3 µH series inductor into a 180 µF low-ESR capacitor at the load, wired with short leads.

equations.name: Feedforward capacitor
equations.note: Its value normally falls between 100 pF and 33 nF.

operation.text: Fixed-frequency PWM at 150 kHz with internal compensation and an internal oscillator. The duty ratio adjusts linearly from 0 to 100 %. Minimum dropout is 1.5 V.

A start-up block and an internal 3.3 V regulator with a 1.23 V reference feed an error amplifier, a PWM comparator against the 150 kHz ramp, a latch and a driver for a Darlington NPN power switch from VIN to OUTPUT. A 44 mΩ resistor in series with the switch feeds two current-limit comparators with 200 mV and 220 mV thresholds. A thermal-shutdown block acts on the driver.

ON/OFF is active low and has hysteresis: below 0.8 V typical the regulator runs, above 1.4 V typical it stops and draws 80 µA typical. An open pin counts as low, so the part runs unless the pin is pulled up. TTL levels can drive it.

The switch current is limited (4 A typical with FEEDBACK at 0 V). If the second current limit trips, the switching frequency falls from 150 kHz to 50 kHz. Thermal shutdown is built in, and power dissipation is internally limited.

On the adjustable version R1 is about 1 kΩ and should be a 1 % part for stability. Above roughly 10 V out a feedforward capacitor CFF across R2 is needed; it also helps with a small input-output difference and when the output capacitor has very little ESR, solid tantalum for example. CFF may be ceramic, plastic film or silver mica; Z5U ceramics are unsuitable because their characteristics drift.

For the fixed versions, inductance and output capacitance are listed against the maximum input voltage; for the adjustable version, output and feedforward capacitors are listed against output voltage. The catch diode is a Schottky with a reverse voltage rating equal to the system's highest input voltage.

CIN and C1 (C1 is optional and reduces input noise) go close to pin 1 and pins 5 to 8. Keep the heavy switching paths short and build them over a ground plane. Run the feedback trace away from the inductor's magnetic field, and put the divider resistors near the FEEDBACK pin with short leads. The GND pins sit outside the loop between the Schottky diode and the output capacitor.
